claims.head: Zibanejad gets company tonight
claims.call: The Maple Leafs’ L2 (Cowan, Matthews and Roslovic) spends at least 54% of its 5-on-5 time against the Rangers’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Maple Leafs keep sending Matthews’s line (Cowan, Matthews and Roslovic) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Hiller has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Rangers’ first line is Perreault, Zibanejad and Lafrenière.

claims.gist: At home, Jim Hiller likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Rangers’ first line.

notes.text: Spencer Martin was added to the roster on Oct 14.

Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 38% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 25% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Chris Tanev is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Darren Raddysh has taken his spot beside Jake McCabe.
John Tavares is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.

TOR.head: A tough matchup for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: The Rangers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but Toronto has home-ice advantage and gets Blankenburg back. The Maple Leafs can pull it off if their power play gets going.

NYR.head: Advantage, the Rangers
NYR.body: The Rangers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but Toronto has home-ice advantage and gets Blankenburg back. The Maple Leafs can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Maple Leafs have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Columbus. The Rangers are 7-3-1.
